title: Streaming vs sync latency correlation hub (model+route p50/p95/p99)
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a consolidated Grafana dashboard and backend metrics plumbing that surfaces p50/p95/p99 latency by model and route, with an explicit breakdown of streaming vs non-streaming requests. The dashboard should let SREs and platform engineers quickly identify regressions tied to model version, route, or serving mode and link directly to traces/spans for root-cause analysis. Work includes metric naming standardization, tagging cardinality limits, tracing hooks to propagate span IDs, and building derived metrics for streaming-first-byte, streaming-final-token, and end-to-end sync completion times.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard shows p50/p95/p99 latency tiles for each model and route (groupable and filterable)
Streaming breakdown: first-byte, mid-stream intervals, and final-token latencies computed and displayed separately from sync end-to-end latency
Each latency datapoint links to a trace view (open trace in Jaeger/Tempo) with consistent span IDs and sampling guidance
Metrics use standardized tags: model, route, model_version, region, deployment_tier and keep cardinality under control
Backend supports queryable histograms or pre-aggregated quantiles so dashboard queries cost remain bounded
Dashboard includes a comparison mode (current window vs baseline) and a simple anomaly flag when p95 increases by >25%
Documentation and runbook updated with steps to onboard new models/routes into the dashboard
comments: 2026-02-26 - Initial design sync: agreed to compute streaming metrics as three separate timers (time-to-first-byte, inter-chunk 95p, time-to-final-token) rather than trying to reconstruct from partial responses. Jin to prototype tracing instrumentation in runtime.

2026-03-02 - Trade-off discussion: opted for pre-aggregated histogram buckets exported from runtime to avoid heavy ad-hoc histogram queries in Grafana. This adds ~1.2% CPU overhead on the runtime in our microbenchmark (acceptable for P1).

2026-03-04 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821 adds trace_id propagation and three new Prometheus metrics with model/route tags. Request: add a low-cardinality 'model_family' tag for high-cardinality models to prevent cardinality explosion.
2026-03-06 - Review feedback from PM (Lina Chen): prefer baseline comparison window to be configurable; added dashboard toggle and default to previous 24h for quick ops checks.
2026-03-09 - Observability infra (Samir Patel) verified pipeline supports new histogram buckets; suggested sampling adjustments to keep telemetry cost neutral for high-traffic routes.

2026-03-10 - Implementation note: streaming final-token latency currently derived from client-observed end event; Jin to patch runtime to emit explicit 'stream.complete' span to avoid clock skew issues.
notes: Key implementation choices: use pre-aggregated histogram export at runtime, low-rate trace sampling with deterministic debug-sampling for flagged requests, limit model_version cardinality by hashing long versions into model_version_short for metrics. Will stage rollout: start with canary routes (alpha) then all-hosted APIs.
next_steps: Merge runtime PR and deploy to canary pool
Update metrics pipeline to accept new histogram buckets and ensure retention in long-term store
Build Grafana panels: model/route table, per-model heatmap, streaming component breakdown charts, and trace drilldown links
Run 48h canary and compare cost/ingestion increases; iterate sampling if needed
